chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Talha ibn Zayd, from one of our companions, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Honor the bread.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and what is its honoring?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When it is placed, do not wait with it for something else.'
And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'And from its honoring is that it should not be trodden upon nor cut (into pieces before it is placed).'
ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for honoring bread according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to highlight the Prophetic etiquette of treating bread with reverence as a fundamental blessing. The instruction to not wait for other dishes emphasizes immediate consumption to prevent waste, while avoiding treading or cutting it prematurely reflects a holistic respect for the physical form of the food. This practice underscores the Shia tradition of viewing daily sustenance as a sacred trust requiring mindful handling.
